analyst_view.overall: Early view: Fulham have steadied under Alvaro Arbeloa after a winless start, unbeaten in four league games (wins over Hull and Coventry, draws at Aston Villa and at home to Newcastle). Brentford under Keith Andrews lost 2-0 at Brighton, where Igor Thiago was sent off for violent conduct; one report says his three-match ban covers Everton, Manchester United and Arsenal, so he should be back for this west London derby.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Fulham's recent games have been tight (1-0, 1-0, 1-1, 1-1) and Arbeloa tends to sit deep once ahead, but Thiago's likely return gives Brentford their main goal threat back. Nothing points clearly either way, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, with Fulham taking more. Fulham play through wide runners like Ryan Sessegnon and push full-backs on, which supports the home share. I see no reason to move off the number this far out.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. It is a local derby, Brentford had a player sent off last time out with Andrews saying Thiago was provoked, and Arbeloa was fined in October for an outburst at officials. I lean a little higher on a tetchy, close game.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots. Fulham's last four league games were all low scoring and Arbeloa's side has protected leads rather than chased more. I lean a bit lower on a cagey derby.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. Fulham were wasteful against Ipswich and Newcastle, but Thiago's likely return lifts Brentford's quality in the box. I stay with the number.
